findings.title: All success criteria are covered by named tasks
findings.description: Cross-reference against the slice design's Success Criteria: (1) "no path reads/writes `adoption.state`, runs detection, spawns `sq`" → 5.1 (file-tree/config snapshot + fake `sq` marker on all four runs), 6.2 greps, 6.3 walkthrough steps 1–2; (2) "Phase 0 brownfield returns the concept prompt and writes nothing" → 5.1 and 6.3; (3) "greenfield/planned/later-phase byte-identical" → 2.1–2.2 captured on unmodified source before any edit, re-checked at 3.3, 3.7 and 6.1; (4) "CLI and MCP `context_build` outputs match" → 5.1 parity check; (5) "`MIN_GUIDE_VERSION` warning still appears" → 3.5, 3.6 and 6.1's named-expectation check; (6) "`services/` imports nothing from `adoption/` or `detection/`" → 3.3 success grep plus 6.2; (7) "no orphan exports (three named exceptions)" → 6.2 export audit; (8) "format/lint/typecheck/tests pass" → 3.7 and 6.1; (9) "269 starts with no build-path code" → sections 3–4. Each Migration Plan row maps to a task (resolver/facts/completion→4.1, contracts→4.2, state writer + `adoption-completed`→4.3, probe→4.4, integrator/factory/engine/type/SectionBuilder→3.1–3.4, node.ts→4.2, CLI→3.5, MCP→3.6). D2's explicit-key check appears in 5.1 as required.

findings.title: Sequencing and dependency order are correct
findings.description: The golden capture (section 2) is explicitly gated before any source edit, matching D6. Within section 3, 3.4 runs `pnpm --filter @context-forge/core build` before 3.5 so `cli`/`mcp-server` see the new `dist/`, and the known-broken window between 3.4 and 3.6 is documented. Deletion order in section 4 is correct: 4.1 removes the three modules before 4.2 trims `contracts.ts`, and 4.2 removes the `ProbeOutcome` import before 4.4 deletes `squadronProbe.ts` that it points at. Section 5 correctly recovers the test deleted in 3.6 via `git show {target}:packages/mcp-server/tests/integration/adoptionParity.test.ts` (the file exists at the target — verified). No circular dependencies. Cited artifacts verified to exist: the two `Comprehension` cases in `SectionBuilder.test.ts`, the adoption-facts block in `ContextTemplateEngine.test.ts`, both guide-warning test names (exact strings match `cli/tests/commands/build.test.ts` and `mcp-server/tests/contextTools.test.ts`), `fixtures/squadron-probe/`, `integrationSetup.ts`, and the `ContextToolOptions` definition plus both `createContextPipeline` call sites.

findings.title: Commit markers are written as checklist items rather than plain `**Commit**:` lines
findings.description: Commit points appear as `- [ ] Commit: …` (3.2a, 3.7, 4.1–4.4, 5.1) and as a checkbox task at 2.3, instead of plain `**Commit**:` lines. The placement itself is right — each sits immediately after a passing test/typecheck success criterion, section 3 deliberately groups commits at 3.2a and 3.7 rather than after every task, and section 6's conditional commit is a tested point. This is a formatting deviation only; AGENTS.md's checklist convention for task files is arguably the reason for the shape.

findings.title: Task 3.6's `integrationSetup.ts` step does not name removal of the `ContextToolOptions` import
findings.description: 3.6 says "drop the `squadronProbe` option and its doc comment" for `mcp-server/tests/helpers/integrationSetup.ts`, but that file also imports `type ContextToolOptions` (line 9) and annotates `createIntegrationClient(options?: ContextToolOptions)` — the type 3.6 deletes outright. A literal reading leaves a dangling import. The task's success criterion (`pnpm --filter @context-forge/mcp typecheck` passes) catches it, so it self-corrects; naming the import explicitly would remove the ambiguity.

findings.title: 6.2's grep list omits the `AdoptionStateWrites` type name
findings.description: The 6.2 grep includes `adoptionStateWrites` (lowercase, the option name) but case-sensitive grep will not match the `AdoptionStateWrites` type defined in `adoptionResolver.ts`. No actual orphan can survive — 4.1 deletes the defining file and 3.3/3.6 remove both importers (`CoreServiceFactory.ts`, `contextTools.ts`) — but the check list does not itself prove it. Adding `AdoptionStateWrites` to the 6.2 pattern would make the verification complete rather than incidental.

structured_findings.summary: All success criteria are covered by named tasks
Sequencing and dependency order are correct
Commit markers are written as checklist items rather than plain `**Commit**:` lines
Task 3.6's `integrationSetup.ts` step does not name removal of the `ContextToolOptions` import
6.2's grep list omits the `AdoptionStateWrites` type name
